dataTypes.what: First name (and optional last name) entered at onboarding, stored in Firestore under the account uid.
Sign-in e-mail (Firebase Auth) for registered accounts. Guests use anonymous auth and give none.
Weight, blood pressure, glucose, symptoms, kick sessions, contractions, hospital bag, pregnancy dates, the first-pregnancy flag, declared medical flags.

Declared conditions (gestational diabetes, hypertension, twin pregnancy), the age range chosen at onboarding, the first-pregnancy flag and the health-data consent record. Age range and first-pregnancy sit on the profile under userProfiles/{uid}, so they are linked to the account.
Appointments (title, date, notes) and reminders stored under the account. The chatbot and the journal PDF keep nothing server side.
Country selected by the user (no location permission is requested). Stored on the profile under userProfiles/{uid}, so it is linked to the account, as in the manifest.

dataTypes.appStoreConnectCategory: Contact Info > Other User Contact Info
dataTypes.what: Emergency contacts (name and phone number) typed in by the user, stored on the profile.
Firebase Auth uid (registered or anonymous) keying every Firestore document; a SHA-256 hash of it is attached to Sentry events.
Sentry crash and error reports, linked to the hashed uid. Only in production builds and only when EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN is set.
Device and OS context attached to every Sentry event.
Sentry.wrap adds a touch boundary, so taps become breadcrumbs on error events. No product analytics SDK is active (firebase analytics is a no-op, src/config/firebase.ts).

ownerChecklist: Re-read each answer in App Store Connect against the published privacy policy (website/privacy.html).

Device ID (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeDeviceID): the native Sentry SDK attaches an installation-scoped default user id to events sent before login (Language, AuthChoice and Login screens), when logger.setUser has not run yet. Read Sentry's and Apple's definitions and either declare Device ID (not used for tracking) or confirm it is out of scope; the manifest does not declare one. Events after login carry the hashed uid instead.
